Name: Requiring on-site nonpotable water reuse systems for certain properties.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring on-site nonpotable water reuse systems for certain properties
BodyName: Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts

Summary: This bill would require certain properties over 100,000 gross square feet to install, operate, and maintain on-site nonpotable water reuse systems. Such properties would be required to obtain a permit from the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene prior to installing or operating such systems. The bill would also require the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) to establish a program to incentivize the installation of on-site nonpotable water reuse systems and other water efficiency technologies on private property. Through the program, DEP would offer grants, water and wastewater fee discounts, and other financial incentives.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 1302.1 of the New York city plumbing code, as amended by local law number 77 for the year 2023, is amended by adding a new section 1302.1.1 to read as follows:
§ 1302.1.1 Where required. An on-site nonpotable water reuse system, installed and operated in accordance with the requirements of this chapter and the terms of the permit required by Section 1301.4, shall be required for any property consisting of: (i) 1 or more buildings on the same tax lot that together exceed 100,000 gross square feet (9,290 m2) or (ii) 1 or more buildings located on 2 or more contiguous tax lots that fall under a singular ownership or management scheme and together exceed 100,000 gross square feet (9,290 m2).

§ 2. Section 1301.4 of the New York city plumbing code, as amended by local law number 77 for the year 2023, is amended to read as follows:
§ 1301.4 Permits. Permits shall be required for the construction, installation, and alteration of nonpotable water systems, and shall be required by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene for review, commissioning, and operation of nonpotable water systems. No permit shall be issued to a property for an on-site nonpotable water reuse system required pursuant to Section 1302.1.1 until documentation has been submitted to the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene containing (i) such property’s estimated nonpotable water demands, (ii) such property’s estimated on-site nonpotable water supplies, (iii) such property’s estimated water savings attributable to such on-site nonpotable water reuse system, and (iv) any other information required by such department. Each permit issued for an on-site nonpotable water reuse system required pursuant to Section 1302.1.1 shall (i) specify required nonpotable water sources and required end use applications for such system and (ii) establish water quality testing and monitoring requirements for such system. Any permit issued pursuant to this section shall be made publicly available on the website of the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene.

§ 3. Subchapter 4 of chapter 3 of title 24 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 24-370 to read as follows:
§ 24-370 Water reuse incentive program. a. Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Department. The term “department” means the department of environmental protection.
On-site nonpotable water reuse system. The term “on-site nonpotable water reuse system” has the same meaning as set forth in section 202 of the New York city plumbing code.
b. Program creation. The department shall create and maintain a program to incentivize installation of fixture retrofits and other water efficiency technologies, such as on-site nonpotable water reuse systems, on private property. Incentives offered through such program may include, but need not be limited to, grants, water fee discounts, and wastewater fee discounts.
c. Program eligibility. The department shall promulgate rules establishing eligibility criteria for the program created pursuant to subdivision b of this section, provided that, in addition to any other eligible properties, a property shall be eligible for such program if such property:
1. Is required to install an on-site nonpotable water reuse system pursuant to section 1302.1.1 of the New York city plumbing code; and
2. Installs, operates, and maintains such on-site nonpotable water reuse system in accordance with the requirements of chapter 13 of the New York city plumbing code. 
§ 4. This local law takes effect 1 year after it becomes law and shall apply to work relating to construction documents filed on and after such date, except that section three of this local law takes effect immediately.
